facts.statement: Campbellodus decipiens was an extinct placoderm fish that lived approximately 380 million years ago during the Late Devonian period.
facts.quote: Campbellodus decipiens is an extinct ptyctodontid placoderm fish that lived around 380 million years ago (Late Devonian).

facts.statement: Fossils of Campbellodus have been found in perfect three-dimensional preservation within the Gogo Formation of Western Australia.
facts.quote: Its fossil remains have been found preserved in perfect three-dimensional form from the Gogo Formation of Western Australia.

facts.statement: The fish possessed very robust tooth plates, with the upper plate featuring a high anterior spine.
facts.quote: The tooth plates are very robust and the upper plate has a high anterior spine.

facts.statement: Campbellodus decipiens is classified as an extinct ptyctodontid placoderm fish.
facts.quote: Campbellodus decipiens is an extinct ptyctodontid placoderm fish

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Campbellodus is Placodermi.
Campbellodus belongs to the class Placodermi.
The genus Campbellodus existed during the Frasnian stage, between 382.31 and 379 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 379 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The species was originally described in 1977 by Miles and Young based on large tooth plates and isolated skull roof bones.
rejected.quote: Originally it was described from large tooth plates and isolated skull roof bones by Miles & Young (1977).
